groups: A direct offline workflow URL expands its ordered functional stages and separately lists planned gaps; the normal binding list contains only the executable stage scope.

The materialization binding shows its four original scores, reasons and source/report links; planned-gap navigation escapes the stage filter without losing workflow context; browser back/forward restores both routes.

Workflow overview reset clears conflicting filters while keeping the route; full reset restores all bindings. Unknown or duplicate route parameters cannot silently select another scope. Priority links open their actual feature bindings.

At 390 CSS pixels the workflow and binding details fit horizontally; light/dark themes produce different backgrounds; keyboard Tab retains a visible focus ring and links hand off focus to their semantic target.
A separate generated fixture renders hostile labels literally, blocks executable file links and initiates no HTTP request. The real atlas data and four-axis scores are untouched.
limitations: Actual Chrome opens generated documentation through file://. The page has no application server or execution backend.
This checks offline mapping navigation, score/evidence display, text safety, narrow layout and focus. It does not rerun the historical product evidence or increase feature maturity.
No Godot, Bevy, installed Tauri, native picker or Android device is exercised. Existing atlas data and scores remain unchanged.
